html:
SMTO-EXE-0222 — This computer's Docker version doesn't work with SMTO

GUID: 4521aa26-c2fc-5bfe-a59a-acd51af1e379
Slug: docker-api-version-incompatible
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO checked Docker on the Gateway computer and found a version it can't work with, either too old or too new, or Docker didn't report its version properly. SMTO stopped before doing anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer which Docker version is installed there. SMTO works with Docker 20.10 and later releases that still accept the connection versions SMTO uses.
  2. If Docker is older than 20.10, have them update Docker on that computer. Older Docker releases can't talk to SMTO at all.
  3. If Docker is recent, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates to update the Gateway, and make sure SMTO itself is up to date. The Docker versions SMTO accepts are built into SMTO, so only a newer SMTO can add support for newer Docker.
  4. Don't change Docker's settings to force a particular connection version. Forcing a version SMTO doesn't support can make Docker requests behave incorrectly.

What success looks like

  • SMTO can show Docker's status on that Gateway without a version message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Docker version number, to the person who installed SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Docker Engine /version response had a missing or malformed ApiVersion or a malformed MinAPIVersion, or the Engine's supported API range does not overlap SMTO's supported range of 1.41 through 1.54.

What this means

  • Engine version metadata was malformed/missing or its supported API interval did not overlap the adapter's range of 1.41 through 1.54. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Engine version metadata was malformed/missing or its supported API interval did not overlap the adapter's range of 1.41 through 1.54.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect ApiVersion and MinAPIVersion from the intended local Engine and compare the supported intersection.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, run docker version against GATEWAY_DOCKER_ENDPOINT and read the Engine's API version and minimum API version. Upgrade an Engine older than API 1.41 (Docker 20.10), or update SMTO and the Gateway if the Engine's minimum API is above 1.54; do not override the negotiated API version.
  • Use a compatible Engine/adapter pair and valid version metadata; do not force an unsupported version.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid version metadata establishes an API version supported by both components.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
